label: Have a screening colonoscopy: colorectal cancer is less likely within 10 years
limits: intention-to-screen: 42.0% of the invited group attended, so this is the effect of an invitation, not of the examination
no significant effect on death from colorectal cancer was shown (risk ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.64–1.16): incidence and mortality are two numbers and this plan claims only the first
one screening round, 10-year follow-up, people aged 55–64 in Poland, Norway, Sweden and the Netherlands; a surveillance interval for someone with adenomas is a different question
a relative change, not an absolute risk: turning it into a percentage for a person needs a baseline this plan does not carry

paper.title: Effect of Colonoscopy Screening on Risks of Colorectal Cancer and Related Death
paper.citation: Bretthauer M, Løberg M, Wieszczy P, et al.; NordICC Study Group. Effect of colonoscopy screening on risks of colorectal cancer and related death. N Engl J Med 2022;387(17):1547–56.

effect.per: invitation to one screening colonoscopy, at 10 years
effect.quote: In intention-to-screen analyses, the risk of colorectal cancer at 10 years was 0.98% in the invited group and 1.20% in the usual-care group, a risk reduction of 18% (risk ratio, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70 to 0.93).

study.population: presumptively healthy men and women aged 55–64 in Poland, Norway, Sweden and the Netherlands
